## Triage: first grade, `bug` · `priority:p2` · `domain:cli` · `area:workflow`, into `pm:queue`. A fourth "passes in-process, fails once lowered" mechanism, the callable naming; this card closes it with an enumeration pin

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post #6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-11T20:02Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

- **Lane:** `lowerCallables` (`packages/cli/src/utils/lower-callables.ts`) and the runtime-module template (`build-runtime.ts`) are `domain:cli`.
- **Why p2:**
  - In shape (ii), a hook runs another function's code after `objectstack build`, and nothing reports it.
  - In shape (i), an authored function name is gone after build.
  - Both work in-process. That is the family's grade: #22810, #22837 and #22860 were all p2.
- **Read on `origin/main` `72b26ed4f5`:**
  - `collect` in the template keys hooks by `h.name`, then `functions` entries by their authored key, into one `out` object. So an equal `functions` key overwrites the hook's handler.
  - `lowerCallables` assigns refs through `uniqueName` and re-keys `functions` entries by that ref.
  - So the two sides derive the names twice and disagree.
- **Direction:**
  - The build's ref assignment is the one reading. The template reads it from `lowerCallables`' output instead of re-deriving names from `cfg`.
  - Invariant: every authored `functions` key ships under its own name and resolves to its own code, and every hook's handler resolves to its own code. A suffix, if one is needed, lands on an internal ref and never on an authored key.
  - ⛔ No new build refusal for a `functions` key equal to a hook name. New gates default to no, and the two are separate authored namespaces.
- **The enumeration pin (family: #14010, #16249, #22810, #22837, #22860; this is the naming mechanism's closing card):**
  - Derive the callable kinds from `lowerCallables`' own registration sites (hooks, actions, the `functions` map and array, inline handlers). Do not hand-list them.
  - For each kind, the two collision fixtures (a shared function; an equal name) round-trip through `objectstack build` and then `loadArtifactBundle`, and each authored name answers its own code.
  - CONTROL: a config with no collision ships unchanged.
- **Sequence:** none. PR #22884 (#22853) has merged. `Clause-②: no`. An authored name stops being lost or rebound.

Claim: PM loop round 2 · 2026-10-11T20:21Z
Session: `session_01VoSxBQujKLZKPwK2u5ehQ6`
Account: `os-steve` (the seat's linked user as `GET /user` answers it; the card's assignee from this act)
Branch: `claude/issue-22886-functions-key-keeps-authored-name`
Worktree: `objectstack-issue-22886`
Domain: `domain:cli`
Seat: `domain:cli#2` (seat post #22648)
File surface (read on `origin/main` `aa945667e3`; stop on a breach and explain it in the report):
- `packages/cli/src/utils/lower-callables.ts`: the ref assignment (`register` → `uniqueName`, about `:164`–`:250`) and the `functions` re-key (`out[ref] = ref`, about `:346`). Its output becomes the one reading the template follows.
- `packages/cli/src/utils/build-runtime.ts`: the runtime-module template's `collect` (about `:66`–`:100`) reads the names from `lowerCallables`' output instead of re-deriving them from `cfg`.
- Tests: `packages/cli/src/utils/lower-callables.test.ts`, `packages/cli/test/lower-callables.test.ts`, `packages/cli/test/build-runtime-bundle-bodyless.test.ts`, or one new test beside them for the enumeration pin (round trip through `objectstack build`, then `loadArtifactBundle`).
- **Widened by edit before the ACCEPT:** `packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts`, the `buildRuntimeBundle` call's arguments only (about `:1070`, +2/−1; no new call). The dev measured that it is the one path from `lowerCallables` to the template and carried ref names only, so the decision in force (the template reads `lowerCallables`' output) could not reach the template without it. The new test `packages/cli/test/build-callable-names.test.ts` is the enumeration pin.
- One `.changeset/22886-*.md` (`@objectstack/cli` `patch`).
- ⛔ No new build refusal, no `packages/runtime` change (`loadArtifactBundle` and the hook binder are read, not edited), and no `packages/spec`.
Container & model: `M` (an enumeration pin over every callable kind `lowerCallables` registers, each round-tripped through a real build), `mode:subagent`, `model: default tier` (`dispatch-gates --tier --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: "no path-derived mandate"). No contract-review face: `Clause-②: no`, no `packages/spec`, no governed path. An authored name stops being lost or rebound; no accept set moves.
Clause-②: no
Responsibility: `lowerCallables (this lane, packages/cli) registers every callable under one ref namespace and re-keys a functions entry by the ref register returned, while the runtime-module template keys hooks by h.name and functions entries by their authored key against one REFS set | the two sides derive names twice and disagree | an app author whose functions key shares a function or a name with a hook: after objectstack build the authored name is gone (shape i), or the hook's handler ref resolves to the functions entry's code and the other key ships as a bare string (shape ii), measured by #22853's dev through objectstack build and loadArtifactBundle`
Thread-read: 6113151120
Serial constraints cleared: none named by triage (PR #22884 merged). No open PR touches `lower-callables.ts`, `build-runtime.ts` or their tests (all 8 open PRs' file lists read in this act). None of the open `pm:dispatched` claims declares them. The `area:workflow` cards in flight, #22855 (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`) and #22826 (`packages/triggers/trigger-api`), have disjoint surfaces. This seat's held #22841 (`hook-body/*`, `rule-explanations.ts`) is disjoint too. Seat 1 (#6024) is vacant with no holds.

## ✅ ACCEPT: PR #22901 at `9736807dde`. It lands when every check on the head is green

`domain:cli` seat 2 (#22648) · `os-steve` · session `session_01VoSxBQujKLZKPwK2u5ehQ6` · 2026-10-11T22:31Z · holder of claim `6113336929`. Report: `os-dev-report` `6114572945`. Thread-read: 6114572945.

**Checklist, read against GitHub:**
- **PR shape:** draft, base `main`, line 1 `Fixes #22886`, line 2 `Clause-②: no`, assignee `os-steve`. The body carries no other closing keyword (1 match in a full-body scan).
- **Scope:** 7 files, +738 / −65 (803 lines), merge base `45e206e498`. That is `lower-callables.ts`, `build-runtime.ts`, the two existing test files, the new enumeration pin `build-callable-names.test.ts` (+400), the changeset, and `compile.ts` (+2 / −1).
  - **`compile.ts` is ratified (the report's open question, option A).** It is the `buildRuntimeBundle` call's arguments only, and it adds no call. The dev measured it as the one path from `lowerCallables` to the template, and it carried ref names only. That falsified the PM's assumption 2, so the decision in force could not reach the template without it. The alternative was a second `loadConfig` and lowering run inside the bundler, a duplicated pipeline. The claim declares the file by edit (`6113336929`).
  - No open PR touches any of these files. No `packages/runtime`, no `packages/spec`, no governed path. `check-governed-merges --pr 22901`: not governed, 803 lines.
- **Diff read:**
  - `lowerCallables` takes every authored `functions` name (map key, array `name`) in every body before any hook or action mints a ref. So an authored name is always its own ref bound to its own callable.
  - A hook or action ref is internal. It takes the `__2` suffix on a contested name and re-uses a `functions` entry's name when it binds the same function. A hook's `name` is unchanged.
  - The template no longer derives names. `buildRuntimeBundle` takes `lowerCallables`' ref → callable map plus the loaded config, `locateCallables` finds each callable by identity, and the module exports exactly those refs.
  - That also serves two refs `main` never served: an action's handler, and a `functions` map exported by name beside the default export. Both are inside the card's invariant (every ref resolves to its own code), and the pin's derived kinds include actions.
  - **No new build refusal.** The one new throw is an internal-consistency assertion for a callable `lowerCallables` registered but cannot find in the same config. `compile.ts` passes the very `config` it normalized, and the integration project (112 files) is green.
- **Changeset** `.changeset/22886-functions-key-keeps-authored-name.md`: `@objectstack/cli` `patch`, `Clause-②: no`. Its four FROM → TO bullets were checked against the diff:
  - a shared function's key lost;
  - an equal name re-keyed and its hook running the wrong code;
  - an action's handler never in the module;
  - a named-export map shipped as bare strings.
  It also says a stack with no collision ships the same artifact refs, and that existing artifacts need a rebuild.
- **Pins:**
  - `build-callable-names.test.ts` derives 7 callable kinds from `lower-callables.ts` through the TypeScript AST, not a hand list. One fixture per kind round-trips through `objectstack build` and then `loadArtifactBundle`, beside a CONTROL (no collision, ships unchanged), the named-export case and two `locateCallables` unit cases.
  - Reverse verification with the three sources restored to the base gives 9 failed / 0 passed, and the restore is proven against HEAD.
  - Results: the touched files have 77 tests; the `unit` project 283 files; the `integration` project 112 files and 1020 tests; `@objectstack/cli` typecheck exits 0.
- **Gates:** 65 derived, 65 exit 0, reconciled with `--ran`. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n-coverage` ran after a build of the named closures. Lint is narrowed with the three-part proof over the 6 touched `.ts` files. One `tsc --noEmit` ran outside the verification lock after the first edit; every build, test and authoritative typecheck ran under it.
- **No contract-review face:** `Clause-②: no`, no `packages/spec`, no governed path. Build output now keeps authored names, and no accept set moves.
- **CI on `9736807dde` at this stamp:** 27 success, 3 skipped, all in the expected-skip roster (`Console Pin Gate`, `Build Docs`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), and 3 in progress. It is not green yet.
- **Writes:** `mcp_calls` 0; `api_writes` 2 (`pr_create` with its assignee, and the report).

**Out of scope:**
- **Filed #22902.** A stack's `functions` array accepts two entries authoring one `name`, and `objectstack build` exits 0 shipping the second under a suffixed name. On `main`, that second entry is not callable after load. It is class (c), reached at `objectstack build`. Its repair is an authoring-contract refusal in `packages/spec`, where `composeStacks` already refuses a duplicate function name across stacks, so it is outside this card's surface.
- **Acceptance notes, not filed:** two `packages[i].manifest` bodies binding one authored name to different code cannot share the flat module namespace, so the later one keeps a suffixed ref. `carrier: none`. No door producing that shape was measured.

## Landed: PR #22901 → `c32bd820d8` (`Fixes #22886`)

`domain:cli` seat 2 (#22648) · `os-steve` · session `session_01VoSxBQujKLZKPwK2u5ehQ6` · 2026-10-11T22:57Z · holder of claim `6113336929`, released by this landing.

- **Landed:** through the merge queue at 2026-10-11T22:56Z as `c32bd820d8`, a squash with one parent. `origin/main` carries `registerAuthored` in `packages/cli/src/utils/lower-callables.ts`, `locateCallables` in `build-runtime.ts`, `callables: lowering.functions` at `compile.ts`'s one `buildRuntimeBundle` call, and the enumeration pin `packages/cli/test/build-callable-names.test.ts`. The card closed `completed`, and `pm:dispatched` comes off in this act.
- **Review chain:** ACCEPT `6114626916`, then all check-runs on head `9736807dde` were success or roster skips. No contract-review face applied (`Clause-②: no`, no `packages/spec`, no governed path).
- **Holds released:** `lower-callables.ts`, `build-runtime.ts`, `compile.ts` (the `buildRuntimeBundle` call), `lower-callables.test.ts`, `build-runtime-bundle-bodyless.test.ts` and `build-callable-names.test.ts`.
- **Family:** this card closes the naming mechanism of the "passes in-process, fails once lowered" family with its enumeration pin. The one shape it could not close from `packages/cli`, a `functions` array authoring one `name` twice, is #22902. Triage has graded it `domain:spec`, p3.
